title: npm test's typecheck starts tsc by its file, not through the missing .bin
body:
## Summary
desk test:types ran a bare `tsc` that resolves through node_modules/.bin; the preflight and kpi-measure check the typescript package, so in every worktree the preflight passed silently and the gate died on "tsc is not recognized".

## Description
Three implementations of "the compiler is there": tools/worktree-preflight.cjs usable() checks node_modules/typescript/package.json, tools/kpi-measure.cjs typecheckErrors() runs node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc, and desk/package.json test:types ran `tsc --noEmit`. A worktree's desk/node_modules is a junction to the main checkout, whose install has no .bin. Repair inside the preflight is impossible without writing into the main checkout (.bin lives in the donor) or replacing the junction with per-package links plus shims (L); detection alone would still leave the gate red. Fixed at the root: test:types starts the compiler by the file the other two check (registry test-harness: platform-quirk-absorption, fix it once in the one wrapper every invocation goes through).

## Flow
- cd <worktree>/desk && npm test
- pretest: preflight sees typescript/package.json through the junction, exit 0, silent
- before: test:types -> 'tsc' is not recognized, exit 1; after: node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc --noEmit, exit 0

## Expected impact
npm test runs in every autopilot and sweep worktree without a manual npm rebuild in the operator's checkout. Nothing writes into the main checkout.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the gate runs wherever the preflight says it can
Before: npm run test:types exit 1 ("tsc not recognized"); preflight exit 0 silent
After: exit 0, 0 error TS lines; new pin in kpi-measure-test red -> green
Method: gate - the pin plus the real script in this worktree
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/package.json:14 (before) "test:types": "tsc --noEmit"
tools/worktree-preflight.cjs:35 usable(): typescript/package.json
tools/kpi-measure.cjs:104 node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc
ls desk/node_modules/.bin -> No such file or directory (junction to C:/Users/kazda/kiro/firetv/desk/node_modules)

title: kpi-measure-test removes its scratch instead of leaving one directory per run
body:
## Summary
The suite made artifacts/kpi-measure/<ms>/ in the tree on every run and never removed it (187 in the main checkout).

## Description
tools/kpi-measure-test.cjs:11 (before) built scratch under artifacts/ and its after() only unlinked links. The five uat suites in tools/ use mkdtemp under the OS temp dir and rmSync. Fixed the same way; links are unlinked one by one first and scratch is removed only when every link is gone, so the recursive remove can never walk a junction (the 2026-10-08 donor-wipe incident).

## Flow
- npm test (kpi-measure-test runs every time)
- before: +1 directory under artifacts/kpi-measure; after: +0, nothing left in temp

## Expected impact
No more scratch pile-up in the tree; git status stays readable. Donor install untouched (verified).

## Evaluation
Claim: other - the suite leaves nothing behind
Before: +1 directory per run (6 -> 7 measured; 187 in the main checkout)
After: +0 (9 -> 9); kpi-measure-* in temp 0 -> 0
Method: probe - counted before and after one run
Result: better
Gate: none

title: kpi-measure's header no longer says nothing it runs writes
body:
## Summary
The header said the suites it runs use their own scratch and "nothing here writes"; the Linga suite it runs leaves artifacts/linga-rules/<ms>/ behind.

## Description
tools/kpi-measure.cjs:3-4 (before). lingaChecks() runs tools/linga-rules-test.cjs, which sets DESK_DATA_DIR under artifacts/linga-rules and never removes it (238 directories in the main checkout). The header now says what is true. The leak itself is linga-rules-test's (another context).

## Flow
- a reader trusts the header and runs npm run measure in a clean tree
- before: told nothing is written; after: told which scratch the suite leaves

## Expected impact
The read-only claim is accurate.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the header matches the code
Before: 1 false claim
After: 0
Method: probe - header read against tools/linga-rules-test.cjs:6
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
tools/kpi-measure.cjs:3-4 (before): "... and nothing here writes."
tools/linga-rules-test.cjs:6 const data=path.resolve(__dirname,'../artifacts/linga-rules',String(Date.now()))

title: kpi-measure bounds the Linga suite and the typecheck it runs, as the rules runner does
body:
## Summary
lingaChecks() and typecheckErrors() spawned the Linga suite and tsc with spawnSync and no timeout; run-rules gives the same suite RULES_SUITE_TIMEOUT_MS.

## Description
tools/run-rules.cjs:20 bounds every suite (default 600000 ms) and reports a timeout as red. tools/kpi-measure.cjs ran the same tools/linga-rules-test.cjs and desk's tsc unbounded, so a stuck child hung npm run measure with no reading. Both now take the same bound, kill on expiry and return the null reading naming the timeout (the tool's own no-reading-is-not-a-zero form). Built in two commits, one per spawn.

## Flow
- a suite or compiler that never exits
- npm run measure
- before: hangs; after: null reading, "timed out after <n> ms"

## Expected impact
A KPI back-measurement always finishes. Real readings unchanged: Linga { pass 110, fail 0 } in 20.8 s, typecheck { errors 0 } in 7.3 s.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - every child the KPI tool waits on is bounded
Before: unbounded suite/compiler spawns: 2
After: 0; two new cases in kpi-measure-test red -> green
Method: gate - fake never-exiting suite and tsc with 400 ms bounds
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
tools/kpi-measure.cjs:71 (before) spawnSync(process.execPath, [linga-rules-test], { encoding: 'utf8' })
tools/kpi-measure.cjs:106 (before) spawnSync(process.execPath, [tsc, '--noEmit', ...], { cwd: desk, encoding: 'utf8' })
tools/run-rules.cjs:20 TIMEOUT = RULES_SUITE_TIMEOUT_MS || 600000

title: A worktree's desk/node_modules is a live junction into the operator's install
body:
## Summary
The preflight links desk/node_modules to the main checkout's install, so any recursive delete in a worktree can empty the operator's desk/node_modules.

## Description
tools/worktree-preflight.cjs ensure() links the whole directory (linkDir, a junction on Windows). The preflight itself only ever unlinks, but every tool downstream sees a real-looking directory: on 2026-10-08 a `git worktree remove --force` walked the junction and emptied the donor (memory: worktree-remove-wipes-donor-node-modules). The same link is why the missing .bin of the donor reached every worktree. Alternatives: npm ci into the worktree (slow, network), a per-worktree directory of per-package junctions plus its own .bin (no write into the donor, still shared packages), or a read-only copy. Each trades disk, time and isolation; the choice changes how every autopilot worktree is provisioned.

## Flow
- a worktree is provisioned by the preflight
- any recursive cleanup that follows reparse points runs in it
- the operator's desk/node_modules is emptied; the main checkout cannot run the desk or the gate

## Expected impact
The operator's install stops being one cleanup away from deletion. Cost: provisioning time or disk per worktree.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a worktree cannot destroy the operator's install
Before: 1 incident (2026-10-08); every worktree shares the donor install read-write through the link
After: unmeasured - depends on the provisioning chosen
Method: simulation - three walked cases: git worktree remove --force (happened), rm -rf desk in a worktree, an npm install run inside the linked directory
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: architecture
evidence:
tools/worktree-preflight.cjs:94 linkDir: fs.symlinkSync(from, to, 'junction')
memory 2026-10-08: a --force remove emptied firetv/desk/node_modules

title: device-rules-test needs tools/node_modules, which the worktree preflight never links
body:
## Summary
Since the A/B drain moved the ink classifier into tools/device.mjs (05980d12) and the relay stub test opened ws clients (fd1f0b5e), desk's rules gate loads pngjs and ws from tools/node_modules; worktree-preflight links only desk/node_modules.

## Description
tools/worktree-preflight.cjs ensure() returns early once desk/node_modules is usable and never looks at tools/. In the sweep worktree device-rules-test went 11 red (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND pngjs, ws) until tools/node_modules was junctioned by hand; then 78 green. The main checkout has tools/ installed, so the operator's gate is green.

## Flow
- autopilot worktree, npm test -> pretest links desk/node_modules only -> device-rules-test imports device.mjs -> pngjs missing -> 11 red
- fix: preflight also links tools/node_modules from the same donor when absent, or device.mjs imports pngjs lazily inside the capture path

## Expected impact
Every autopilot worktree's npm test reads green again without a hand junction.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the gate runs in a worktree
Before: device-rules-test 11 of 11 red in a worktree without tools/node_modules
After: 0 red with tools/node_modules linked (measured by hand)
Method: probe - the hand junction is the fix's own shape
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'pngjs' imported from tools/device.mjs; Error: Cannot find module 'ws'
tools/worktree-preflight.cjs ensure(): if (usable(dest)) return { action: "present", dest };
instrument: kpi-measure-test style case: a fake checkout with desk/ linked and tools/ absent, preflight run, require device.mjs

title: calc-rules-test went red once under a full parallel run-rules and is green alone
body:
## Summary
The harness worker's full run-rules had calc-rules-test red (1 of 1753); it is green 3 of 3 alone on two trees.

## Description
Same shape as engines case 23 (fixed 28e1f42f): a suite that passes alone and fails under load usually holds a wall-clock bound or a shared temp path. Not yet located.

## Flow
- run-rules runs 78 suites in parallel -> calc-rules-test red once -> alone green

## Expected impact
A red gate nobody caused stops costing a rerun and a doubt.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the gate is deterministic
Before: 1 red in 1 loaded run, 0 in 3 idle
After: unknown
Method: simulation - one observation
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence: harness worker run-rules: 76 green, 1 red (calc-rules-test); tip runs 1, 2 and branch run: exit 0
instrument: run calc-rules-test 32x beside CPU burners, as 28e1f42f measured case 23; grep it for Date.now/setTimeout bounds and shared temp dirs
